manualTranslations.zh: 中統元年，世祖即位，廉希憲、商挺奏以為成都經略使總管萬戶。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, when Shizu took the throne, Lian Xixian and Shang Ting memorialized that he be made Chengdu commissioner for frontier strategy and commander of ten thousand households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong (1260), when Kublai took the throne, Lian Xixian and Shang Ting recommended appointing him Chengdu commissioner for frontier strategy and commander of ten thousand households.

manualTranslations.zh: 宋瀘州守將劉整密送款求降，黑馬遣元振往受之。
manualTranslations.literal: The Song defending commander of Luzhou, Liu Zheng, secretly sent overtures seeking surrender, and Heima dispatched Yuanzhen to receive it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Song commander of Luzhou, Liu Zheng, secretly sent overtures of surrender, and Heima sent Yuanzhen to receive them.

manualTranslations.zh: 諸將皆曰：「劉整無故而降，不可信也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The generals all said: "Liu Zheng is surrendering without cause—it cannot be trusted."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The generals all said, "Liu Zheng is surrendering without cause. This cannot be trusted."

manualTranslations.zh: 元振曰：「宋權臣當國，賞罰無章，有功者往往以計除之，是以將士離心；
manualTranslations.literal: Yuanzhen said: "Powerful Song ministers hold the state; rewards and punishments are erratic, and men of merit are often removed by stratagem, so officers and soldiers are disaffected;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen said, "Powerful Song ministers control the government. Rewards and punishments are erratic, and meritorious men are often removed by intrigue, so the officers and soldiers are disaffected;

manualTranslations.zh: 且整本非南人，而居瀘南重地，事勢與李全何異，整此舉無可疑者。」
manualTranslations.literal: moreover, Zheng is originally not a southerner yet holds a vital post south of Luzhou—the situation is no different from Li Quan's. There is nothing doubtful in this act of Zheng."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: moreover, Zheng is not originally a southerner yet holds a vital post south of Luzhou—the situation is no different from Li Quan's. There is nothing suspicious in this move."

manualTranslations.zh: 遂行。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he set out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thereupon he set out.

manualTranslations.zh: 黑馬戒之曰：「劉整，宋之名將，瀘乃蜀之衝要，今整遽以瀘降，情偽不可知，汝無為一身慮，事成則為國家之利，不成則當效死，乃其分也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Heima admonished him, saying: "Liu Zheng is a famous Song general. Luzhou is the strategic gateway of Shu. Now Zheng has suddenly offered Luzhou in surrender, and whether his intent is genuine cannot be known. Do not worry for yourself alone. If the affair succeeds it will benefit the state; if it fails you should die in the attempt—that is your duty."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heima warned him: "Liu Zheng is a famous Song general, and Luzhou is the strategic gateway of Sichuan. Now he has suddenly offered Luzhou in surrender, and his intent cannot be known. Do not worry only for yourself. If the affair succeeds it will benefit the state; if it fails you must die in the attempt—that is your duty."

manualTranslations.zh: 元振至瀘，整開門出迎，元振棄眾而先下馬，與整相見，示以不疑。
manualTranslations.literal: When Yuanzhen reached Luzhou, Zheng opened the gate to welcome him. Yuanzhen left his escort and dismounted first, met with Zheng, and showed that he did not doubt him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yuanzhen reached Luzhou, Zheng opened the gate to welcome him. Yuanzhen left his escort, dismounted first, met Zheng, and showed that he trusted him.

manualTranslations.zh: 明日，請入城，元振釋戎服，從數騎，與整聯轡而入，飲燕至醉，整心服焉。
manualTranslations.literal: The next day, invited into the city, Yuanzhen put off his armor, took only a few horsemen, and entered riding bridle to bridle with Zheng. They feasted until drunk, and Zheng submitted in heart.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The next day he was invited into the city. Yuanzhen set aside his armor, took only a few horsemen, and entered riding bridle to bridle with Zheng. They feasted until drunk, and Zheng was won over.

manualTranslations.zh: 獻金六千兩、男女五百人，元振以金分賜將士，而歸還其男女。
manualTranslations.literal: Zheng presented six thousand taels of gold and five hundred men and women. Yuanzhen distributed the gold among the officers and soldiers and returned the men and women.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zheng presented six thousand taels of gold and five hundred captives. Yuanzhen distributed the gold among his officers and soldiers and returned the people.

manualTranslations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Kan memorialized with twenty-five proposals on establishing the dynastic title, building the capital, setting up the secretariats and censorate, founding schools, and other matters, as well as a strategy for pacifying Song. The gist was: "Song holds the southeast and makes Wu and Yue its home; its vital ground is only Jing and Xiang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Kublai took the throne, Kan submitted a memorial outlining twenty-five proposals on establishing the dynastic title, building the capital, setting up the secretariats and censorate, founding schools, and other matters, together with a strategy for conquering Song. The gist was: "Song holds the southeast and treats Wu and Yue as its home. Its vital ground is only Jing and Xiang.

manualTranslations.zh: 今日之計，當先取襄陽，既克襄陽，彼揚、廬諸城，彈丸地耳，置之勿顧，而直趨臨安，疾雷不及掩耳，江淮、巴蜀不攻自平。」
manualTranslations.literal: The plan for today should be to take Xiangyang first. Once Xiangyang is captured, the cities of Yang and Lu are but pellets of earth—leave them and pay no heed, but drive straight for Lin'an. Thunder will not outpace the covering of ears; the Jiang-Huai and Ba-Shu regions will submit without being attacked."

sourceRange.text: 中統元年，廉希憲、商挺宣撫川、陝，時密力火者握重兵，居成都，希憲與挺慮其為變，以黑馬有膽智，使乘驛矯詔竟誅之。其子訴于朝，世祖諭之曰：「茲朕命也，其勿復言。」三年，命兼成都路軍民經略使。瀘州被圍，黑馬已屬疾，猶親督轉輸不輟，左右諫其少休，黑馬曰：「國事方急，以此死，無憾。」遂卒，年六十三。累贈太傅，封秦國公，諡忠惠。子十二人，元振、元禮顯。

manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, Lian Xixian and Shang Ting pacified and reassured Sichuan and Shaanxi. At the time Mizilihuozhe held heavy troops and resided at Chengdu. Xixian and Ting feared he would rebel and, because Heima had courage and wit, had him travel by post relay with a forged edict and execute him to the end.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong (1260), Lian Xixian and Shang Ting were sent to pacify Sichuan and Shaanxi. Mizilihuozhe then held heavy forces at Chengdu. Fearing he might rebel, Xixian and Ting, trusting Heima's courage and wit, had him travel by courier with a forged edict and put Mizilihuozhe to death.

manualTranslations.zh: 其子訴于朝，世祖諭之曰：「茲朕命也，其勿復言。」
manualTranslations.literal: His son appealed at court. Shizu instructed him, saying: "This was My command. Speak of it no more."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son appealed at court. Kublai told him, "This was My command. Say no more of it."

manualTranslations.zh: 三年，命兼成都路軍民經略使。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year he was ordered to serve concurrently as commissioner for the military and civil administration of the Chengdu circuit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third year (1262) he was appointed concurrently commissioner for the military and civil administration of the Chengdu circuit.

manualTranslations.zh: 瀘州被圍，黑馬已屬疾，猶親督轉輸不輟，左右諫其少休，黑馬曰：「國事方急，以此死，無憾。」
manualTranslations.literal: When Luzhou was besieged, Heima was already near death, yet still personally directed transport without pause. Those beside him urged him to rest a little. Heima said: "State affairs are urgent. To die thus is without regret."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Luzhou was besieged, Heima was already gravely ill, yet still personally directed supply transport without pause. Those around him urged him to rest. Heima said, "State affairs are urgent. To die in this service is no regret."

manualTranslations.zh: 遂卒，年六十三。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he died, aged sixty-three.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-three.

manualTranslations.zh: 累贈太傅，封秦國公，諡忠惠。
manualTranslations.literal: He was posthumously honored repeatedly as Grand Tutor, enfeoffed as Duke of Qin, and given the posthumous title Zhonghui.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor, enfeoffed as Duke of Qin, and given the posthumous name Zhonghui, "Loyal and Gracious."

manualTranslations.zh: 子十二人，元振、元禮顯。
manualTranslations.literal: He had twelve sons; Yuanzhen and Yuanli were the most prominent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He had twelve sons; Yuanzhen and Yuanli were the most notable.

sourceRange.text: 至元元年，遷潼川路漢軍都元帥。二年九月，宋制置夏貴率軍五萬犯潼川，元禮所領纔數千，眾寡不敵，諸將登城望貴軍，有懼色。元禮曰：「料敵制勝，在智不在力。」乃出戰，屢破之，復大戰蓬溪，自寅至未，勝負不決，激厲將士曰：「此去城百里，為敵所乘，則城不可得入，潼川非國家有矣。丈夫當以死戰取功名，時不可失也。」即持長刀，大呼突入陣，所向披靡，將士咸奮，無一不當百，大敗貴兵，斬首萬餘級，生擒千餘人。捷奏，賜錦衣二襲、白金三錠、名馬一匹、金鞍轡、弓矢，召入朝，命復還潼川，立蓬溪寨。

manualTranslations.zh: 至元元年，遷潼川路漢軍都元帥。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan he was transferred to supreme commander of the Han armies of the Tongchuan circuit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiyuan (1264) he was made supreme commander of the Han armies of the Tongchuan circuit.

manualTranslations.zh: 二年九月，宋制置夏貴率軍五萬犯潼川，元禮所領纔數千，眾寡不敵，諸將登城望貴軍，有懼色。
manualTranslations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year, the Song commissioner Xia Gui led fifty thousand troops to invade Tongchuan. The force Yuanli commanded was only a few thousand; the odds were unequal, and the generals mounting the wall to look on Xia Gui's army showed fear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year (1265), the Song commissioner Xia Gui led fifty thousand troops against Tongchuan. Yuanli commanded only a few thousand men. Outnumbered, the generals on the wall looking down at Xia Gui's army showed fear.

manualTranslations.zh: 元禮曰：「料敵制勝，在智不在力。」
manualTranslations.literal: Yuanli said: "To measure the enemy and prevail lies in wit, not in strength."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuanli said, "Defeating the enemy depends on wit, not strength."

manualTranslations.zh: 乃出戰，屢破之，復大戰蓬溪，自寅至未，勝負不決，激厲將士曰：「此去城百里，為敵所乘，則城不可得入，潼川非國家有矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he gave battle, repeatedly defeated them, and fought again at great length at Pengxi. From yin to wei the outcome was undecided. He roused the officers and soldiers, saying: "This place is one hundred li from the city. If the enemy presses us, the city cannot be re-entered, and Tongchuan will no longer belong to the state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He went out to fight, repeatedly defeated them, and fought a major battle at Pengxi. From yin to wei the outcome remained in doubt. He roused his officers and soldiers, saying, "We are one hundred li from the city. If the enemy presses us, we cannot get back in, and Tongchuan will be lost to the state.

manualTranslations.zh: 丈夫當以死戰取功名，時不可失也。」
manualTranslations.literal: A man should win fame by fighting to the death. The moment must not be lost."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A man should win honor by fighting to the death. This moment must not be lost."

manualTranslations.zh: 即持長刀，大呼突入陣，所向披靡，將士咸奮，無一不當百，大敗貴兵，斬首萬餘級，生擒千餘人。
manualTranslations.literal: Immediately grasping a long blade, he shouted and plunged into the formation. Wherever he turned the enemy broke before him. Officers and soldiers all took heart; not one failed to fight as if worth a hundred. Xia Gui's army was routed utterly; more than ten thousand heads were taken and more than one thousand men captured alive.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Seizing a long blade, he shouted and charged into the enemy ranks. Wherever he turned the enemy broke before him. His officers and soldiers took heart; each fought as if worth a hundred. Xia Gui's army was routed. More than ten thousand heads were taken and more than one thousand men captured alive.

manualTranslations.zh: 捷奏，賜錦衣二襲、白金三錠、名馬一匹、金鞍轡、弓矢，召入朝，命復還潼川，立蓬溪寨。
manualTranslations.literal: When victory was reported he was granted two suits of brocade robes, three ingots of white metal, one famous horse, a gold saddle and bridle, and bow and arrows. He was summoned to court, ordered to return to Tongchuan, and established Pengxi Stockade.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When victory was reported he received two brocade robes, three ingots of silver, a fine horse, a gold saddle and bridle, and bow and arrows. He was summoned to court, ordered back to Tongchuan, and established Pengxi Stockade.

sourceRange.text: 」至大元年，遷太子詹事，兼衞率使。俄拜中書左丞，仍平章政事，商議中書省事。未幾，擢河南行省平章政事，佩金虎符，提調屯田事，帝召至榻前，面諭曰：「汴省事重，屯田久廢，卿當為國竭力。」賜黑貂裘一、錦衣二襲。瑋至汴，建諸葛亮祠，立書院，以地三千畝贍之。三年，改河南行尚書省平章政事，卒。贈太傅、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封梁國公，諡文正。

context.beforeSource: 」瑋出拜，帝曰：「朕知卿能以忠直為國，朕有不逮，卿當勉輔。
context.afterSource: 李守賢字才叔，大寧義州人也。
context.beforeLocal: 瑋出拜，帝曰：「朕知卿能以忠直為國，朕有不逮，卿當勉輔。
context.afterLocal: 李守賢字才叔，大寧義州人也。

manualTranslations.zh: 至大元年，遷太子詹事，兼衞率使。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was transferred to Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household and concurrently made Commissioner of the Guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first Zhide year he was made Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household and concurrently Commissioner of the Guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 俄拜中書左丞，仍平章政事，商議中書省事。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon he was appointed Left Vice Councillor of the Central Secretariat, again made Pacification Commissioner, and charged to deliberate on Central Secretariat affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed left vice councillor of the Central Secretariat, again made pacification commissioner, and charged with Central Secretariat affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 未幾，擢河南行省平章政事，佩金虎符，提調屯田事，帝召至榻前，面諭曰：「汴省事重，屯田久廢，卿當為國竭力。」
manualTranslations.literal: Before long he was elevated to Pacification Commissioner of the Henan Branch Secretariat, bore a golden tiger tally, and was put in charge of garrison-farm affairs. The emperor summoned him before the couch and instructed him face to face, saying, "The affairs of Bian are weighty, and garrison farming has long lain idle; you must strive with all your strength for the state."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before long he was elevated to pacification commissioner of the Henan Branch Secretariat, given a golden tiger tally, and put in charge of garrison farming. The emperor summoned him to his couch and said in person, "Bian's affairs are weighty and garrison farming has long lain idle. You must serve the state with all your strength."

manualTranslations.zh: 賜黑貂裘一、錦衣二襲。
manualTranslations.literal: He was granted one black sable fur coat and two suits of brocade robes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was granted one black sable coat and two brocade suits.

manualTranslations.zh: 瑋至汴，建諸葛亮祠，立書院，以地三千畝贍之。
manualTranslations.literal: When Wei reached Bian he built a shrine to Zhuge Liang, established an academy, and endowed it with three thousand mu of land.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Wei reached Bian he built a shrine to Zhuge Liang, founded an academy, and endowed it with three thousand mu of land.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年，改河南行尚書省平章政事，卒。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year he was changed to Pacification Commissioner of the Henan Branch Secretariat of the Ministry of Revenue and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made pacification commissioner of the Henan Branch Secretariat of the Ministry of Revenue and died.

manualTranslations.zh: 贈太傅、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封梁國公，諡文正。
manualTranslations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Tutor, Commissioner with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, and Supreme Pillar of State; enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Liang; posthumous title Wenzheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor, Commissioner with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, and Supreme Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Liang with the posthumous title Wenzheng.

sourceRange.text: 中統元年，詔立十道宣慰司，以瑨為順天宣慰使。至元元年，轉淄萊路總管。六年，改太原路總管。十二年，陞燕南道提刑按察使。十四年，遷河南道。十六年，致仕。明年卒，年八十。皇慶元年，贈儀同三司、太保、上柱國，追封定國公，諡襄穆。子秉溫。

manualTranslations.literal: His son Mieligan at first served directly in palace guard duty, inherited his father's post, led troops to garrison Guangdong, then was transferred to garrison Huizhou and pacified the bandits Tan Daliao, Zhu Zhen, and others.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Mieligan first served in palace guard duty, succeeded to his father's post, and led troops to garrison Guangdong. He was soon transferred to Huizhou, where he suppressed the bandits Tan Daliao, Zhu Zhen, and others.

manualTranslations.zh: 元貞元年，移戍袁州，盜陀頭以眾犯境，悉剿除之。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen he was transferred to garrison Yuan Prefecture; the bandit Tuotou invaded the border with a host, and he utterly exterminated them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Yuanzhen 1 (1295) he was posted to Yuan Prefecture. When the bandit Tuotou invaded with a large force, he exterminated them entirely.

manualTranslations.zh: 尋廣之南恩盜起，復領兵平之。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon bandits arose in Nan'en in Guangdong; he again led troops and pacified them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon after, bandits rose in Nan'en in Guangdong, and he again led troops to suppress them.

manualTranslations.zh: 還，沒于袁州。
manualTranslations.literal: On his return he died at Yuan Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On his return he died at Yuan Prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 贈懷遠大將軍、季陽萬戶府萬戶、輕車都尉、渤海郡侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand Far-Reaching General, myriarch of the Jiyang Myriarchate, Commandant of Light Chariots, and Marquis of Bohai Commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles Grand Far-Reaching General, myriarch of the Jiyang Myriarchate, Commandant of Light Chariots, and Marquis of Bohai Commandery.

sourceRange.text: 忱字允中，幼讀書，明敏有才識。平章趙璧引見裕宗潛邸，語稱旨，命宿衞，掌錢穀計簿。授山北遼東道提刑按察司副使。駙馬伯忽里數馳獵蹂民田，忱以法繩之。憲吏耿熙言徵北京宣慰司積年逋負，計可得鈔二十萬錠。帝遣使覈實。熙懼事露，擅增制語，有「并打算大小一切諸衙門等事」凡十二字，追繫官吏至數百人。忱驗問，知其詐，熙乃款伏。裕宗薨于潛邸，忱建言：「陛下春秋高，當早建儲嗣。」平章不忽木以聞，帝嘉納焉。改河北河南道提刑按察副使。忱以江南人鬻子北方，名為養子，實為奴也，乞禁之。又省部以正軍餘田出調發，忱言：「士卒衝冒寒暑，遠涉江海，宜加優恤。」皆從之。潁州朱喜，嘗俘於兵，既自贖，主家利其貲，復欲以為奴。又有誣息州汪清為奴，殺而奪其妻子及田宅者。獄久不決，忱皆正之。劾罷鎮南帥唐兀台，唐兀台結援大臣，誣奏于帝，繫忱至京師，得面陳其事，世祖大悟，抵唐兀台罪。按察司改廉訪司，起忱為燕南河北道肅政廉訪副使，累遷嶺南廣西、河東山西兩道肅政廉訪使，江陵、汴梁兩路總管。至大（三）〔元〕年，拜中奉大夫、雲南行省參知政事，未行，卒。

manualTranslations.zh: 忱字允中，幼讀書，明敏有才識。
manualTranslations.literal: Chen, courtesy name Yunzhong, read books from youth; he was keen, clever, and talented.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chen, styled Yunzhong, studied from childhood. Keen and clever, he showed real talent and judgment.

manualTranslations.zh: 平章趙璧引見裕宗潛邸，語稱旨，命宿衞，掌錢穀計簿。
manualTranslations.literal: Grand Councillor Zhao Bi introduced him at Prince Zong's residence before enthronement; his words pleased the prince, who ordered him to palace guard duty and put him in charge of revenue and grain account books.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Zhao Bi introduced him at Prince Zong's pre-enthronement residence. His words pleased the prince, who assigned him to palace guard duty and put him in charge of revenue and grain accounts.

manualTranslations.zh: 授山北遼東道提刑按察司副使。
manualTranslations.literal: He was appointed Vice Intendant of the Judicial Investigation Commission for the North-of-the-Mountains and Liaodong Circuit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Intendant of the Judicial Investigation Commission for the North-of-the-Mountains and Liaodong Circuit.

manualTranslations.zh: 駙馬伯忽里數馳獵蹂民田，忱以法繩之。
manualTranslations.literal: The imperial son-in-law Bohuli repeatedly rode out hunting and trampled the people's fields; Chen restrained him according to law.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The imperial son-in-law Bohuli repeatedly hunted across the countryside and trampled farmers' fields. Chen held him accountable under the law.

manualTranslations.zh: 憲吏耿熙言徵北京宣慰司積年逋負，計可得鈔二十萬錠。
manualTranslations.literal: Surveillance clerk Geng Xi stated that collecting long-standing arrears of the Beiping Pacification Commission would yield an estimated two hundred thousand ding of paper money.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Surveillance clerk Geng Xi reported that collecting long-standing arrears owed to the Beiping Pacification Commission would yield an estimated two hundred thousand ding of paper money.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝遣使覈實。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy to verify this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy to verify the claim.

manualTranslations.zh: 熙懼事露，擅增制語，有「并打算大小一切諸衙門等事」凡十二字，追繫官吏至數百人。
manualTranslations.literal: Geng, fearing exposure, on his own authority added to the imperial rescript the twelve characters "and calculate matters large and small of every yamen alike," and had officials pursued and imprisoned by the hundreds.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Geng, fearing exposure, on his own authority added twelve characters to the imperial rescript—"and calculate matters large and small of every yamen alike"—and had officials pursued and imprisoned by the hundreds.

manualTranslations.zh: 忱驗問，知其詐，熙乃款伏。
manualTranslations.literal: Chen examined and questioned him, discovered the fraud, and Geng then fully confessed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chen investigated and questioned him, uncovered the fraud, and Geng then confessed fully.

manualTranslations.zh: 裕宗薨于潛邸，忱建言：「陛下春秋高，當早建儲嗣。」
manualTranslations.literal: When Prince Zong died at the residence before enthronement, Chen proposed: "Your Majesty's years are advanced; you should establish an heir early."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Prince Zong died at the pre-enthronement residence, Chen proposed, "Your Majesty's years are advanced; you should establish an heir early."

manualTranslations.zh: 平章不忽木以聞，帝嘉納焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Grand Councillor Buqumu reported this, and the emperor gladly accepted it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Buqumu reported this to the throne, and the emperor gladly accepted the advice.

manualTranslations.zh: 改河北河南道提刑按察副使。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Intendant of the Judicial Investigation Commission for the Hebei-Henan Circuit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Intendant of the Judicial Investigation Commission for the Hebei-Henan Circuit.

manualTranslations.zh: 忱以江南人鬻子北方，名為養子，實為奴也，乞禁之。
manualTranslations.literal: Chen said that people from Jiangnan sold their sons in the north, calling it adoption but in reality making them slaves, and requested a ban.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chen argued that people from Jiangnan sold their sons in the north under the name of adoption but in reality as slaves, and requested a ban.

manualTranslations.zh: 又省部以正軍餘田出調發，忱言：「士卒衝冒寒暑，遠涉江海，宜加優恤。」
manualTranslations.literal: Furthermore, when the provincial and central ministries levied supplies from surplus lands of regular troops, Chen said: "Soldiers brave heat and cold and travel far across rivers and seas; they should receive added favorable treatment."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the provincial and central ministries levied supplies from surplus lands held by regular troops, Chen said, "Soldiers brave heat and cold and travel far across rivers and seas; they deserve added favorable treatment."

manualTranslations.zh: 皆從之。
manualTranslations.literal: All were accepted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: All his proposals were accepted.

manualTranslations.zh: 潁州朱喜，嘗俘於兵，既自贖，主家利其貲，復欲以為奴。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhu Xi of Ying Prefecture had once been captured in warfare; after he redeemed himself, his master coveted his property and wanted to make him a slave again.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi of Ying Prefecture had once been taken captive in war. After he redeemed himself, his master coveted his property and tried to enslave him again.

manualTranslations.zh: 又有誣息州汪清為奴，殺而奪其妻子及田宅者。
manualTranslations.literal: There were also those who falsely accused Wang Qing of Xi Prefecture of being a slave, killed him, and seized his wife, children, fields, and house.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: There were also cases in which men falsely accused Wang Qing of Xi Prefecture of being a slave, killed him, and seized his wife, children, fields, and house.

manualTranslations.zh: 獄久不決，忱皆正之。
manualTranslations.literal: The cases long went unresolved; Chen rectified them all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The cases had long gone unresolved; Chen set them all right.

manualTranslations.zh: 劾罷鎮南帥唐兀台，唐兀台結援大臣，誣奏于帝，繫忱至京師，得面陳其事，世祖大悟，抵唐兀台罪。
manualTranslations.literal: He impeached and removed the Commander of Pacifying the South Tang'utai; Tang'utai allied with powerful ministers and falsely memorialized the emperor; Chen was imprisoned and brought to the capital, but was able to state the matter in person; Kublai suddenly understood and punished Tang'utai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He impeached and removed the Commander of Pacifying the South, Tang'utai. Tang'utai allied with powerful ministers and falsely memorialized the emperor. Chen was imprisoned and brought to the capital, but was able to state the matter in person. Kublai suddenly understood and punished Tang'utai.

manualTranslations.zh: 按察司改廉訪司，起忱為燕南河北道肅政廉訪副使，累遷嶺南廣西、河東山西兩道肅政廉訪使，江陵、汴梁兩路總管。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Investigation Commission was renamed the Surveillance Commission, Chen was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Surveillance Commission for the Yannan-Hebei Circuit, and successively promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Lingnan-Guangxi and Hedong-Shanxi circuits, and overall administrator of the Jiangling and Bianliang routes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Investigation Commission was renamed the Surveillance Commission, Chen was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Yannan-Hebei Surveillance Commission. He was later promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of the Lingnan-Guangxi and Hedong-Shanxi circuits and overall administrator of the Jiangling and Bianliang routes.

manualTranslations.zh: 至大三年，拜中奉大夫、雲南行省參知政事，未行，卒。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year of Zhida he was appointed Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Vice Director of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat; before he could depart, he died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Zhida 3 (1310) he was appointed Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Vice Director of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat, but died before he could take up the post.

manualTranslations.literal: In the year guiyou Taizu sent troops to break Zijing Pass; Rou submitted with his following; Branch Secretariat Ba Zha reported it and Rou was made chief official of Zhuo and Yi prefectures, wearing a gold tally.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 1213 Taizu sent troops to break Zijing Pass. Rou submitted with his men. Ba Zha of the branch secretariat reported the matter, and Rou was made chief official of Zhuo and Yi prefectures with a gold tally.

manualTranslations.zh: 丙戌，羣盜並起，柔單騎徧入諸柵，說降其眾，以功遷龍虎衞上將軍、真定涿等路兵馬都元帥，佩金虎符，兼銀冶總管。
manualTranslations.literal: In bingxu bandits rose everywhere together; Rou alone on horseback went through all the stockades persuading their crowds to submit; for merit he was transferred to Grand General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and overall marshal of horse and foot forces of the Zhending-Zhuo circuits, wearing a gold tiger tally and concurrently serving as silver-smelting commissioner.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 1226 bandits rose on every side. Rou rode alone through the stockades and talked their men into submission. For this he was made Grand General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and overall marshal of the Zhending and Zhuo circuits, with a gold tiger tally and concurrent charge as silver-smelting commissioner.

manualTranslations.zh: 庚寅，太宗命兼管諸處打捕總管。
manualTranslations.literal: In gengyin Taizong ordered him to concurrently oversee the hunt-and-capture commissioners of all places.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 1230 Taizong also put him in charge of the hunt-and-capture commissioners throughout the realm.

manualTranslations.zh: 丙申，加金紫光祿大夫，卒。
manualTranslations.literal: In bingshen he was given Gold-Purple Grand Master of Glorious Blessings and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 1236 he was promoted to Gold-Purple Grand Master of Glorious Blessings and died.

manualTranslations.zh: 至順元年，追封天水郡公，諡莊靖。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui Commandery with the posthumous title Zhuangjing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 1330 he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui with the posthumous title Zhuangjing.

manualTranslations.zh: 曾孫世安，榮祿大夫、江西行省左丞。
manualTranslations.literal: His great-grandson Shi'an was Grand Master of Glorious Blessings and left associate administrator of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Shi'an served as Grand Master of Glorious Blessings and left associate administrator of the Jiangxi branch secretariat.

manualTranslations.literal: Tianlu inherited the title; the Prince of Lu acting by order appointed him Grand General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, Superior General of Dongping, and marshal of the Dongping Circuit, wearing a gold tiger tally.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tianlu inherited the rank. The Prince of Lu, acting by order, made him Grand General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, superior general of Dongping, and marshal of the Dongping circuit, with a gold tiger tally.

sourceRange.text: 子復亨，襲為行軍千戶，從嚴實略安豐、通、泰、淮、濠、泗、蘄、黃、安慶諸州。憲宗西征，復亨攝萬戶，統東平軍馬攻釣魚山苦竹寨，有功，師還，兼德州軍民總管。中統元年，奉旨戍和林，還，授虎符，進武衞軍副都指揮使。李璮叛，遣使招復亨，復亨立斬之。時遣兵討賊，集濟南，乏食，復亨盡出其私蓄以濟師，世祖嘉之，賜白金五千兩，復亨固辭。

context.beforeSource: 歲丙辰卒。
context.afterSource: 至元二年，進左翼侍衞親軍都指揮使。
context.beforeLocal: 歲丙辰卒。
context.afterLocal: 至元二年，進左翼侍衛親軍都指揮使。

manualTranslations.zh: 子復亨，襲為行軍千戶，從嚴實略安豐、通、泰、淮、濠、泗、蘄、黃、安慶諸州。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Fuheng inherited as campaign thousand-household and followed Yan Shi in reducing Anfeng, Tong, Tai, Huai, Hao, Si, Qi, Huang, and Anqing prefectures.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Fuheng inherited the post of campaign thousand-household and followed Yan Shi in campaigns across Anfeng, Tong, Tai, Huai, Hao, Si, Qi, Huang, and Anqing.

manualTranslations.zh: 憲宗西征，復亨攝萬戶，統東平軍馬攻釣魚山苦竹寨，有功，師還，兼德州軍民總管。
manualTranslations.literal: On Emperor Xianzong's western campaign Fuheng acted as ten-thousand-household, commanded Dongping horse and foot forces to attack the Kuzhu stockade at Diaoyu Mountain, had merit, and when the army returned he was made concurrent overall commander of troops and civilians in Dezhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On Xianzong's western campaign Fuheng served as acting ten-thousand-household, led Dongping forces against the Kuzhu stockade at Diaoyu Mountain, and distinguished himself. When the army returned he was also made overall commander of Dezhou's troops and civilians.

manualTranslations.zh: 中統元年，奉旨戍和林，還，授虎符，進武衞軍副都指揮使。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, by imperial order he garrisoned Karakorum; returning, he was granted a tiger tally and advanced to vice commander of the Martial Guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 1260 he was ordered to garrison Karakorum. On his return he received a tiger tally and was promoted to vice commander of the Martial Guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 李璮叛，遣使招復亨，復亨立斬之。
manualTranslations.literal: Li Tan rebelled, sent envoys to recruit Fuheng, and Fuheng immediately beheaded them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Li Tan rebelled he sent envoys to win Fuheng over, but Fuheng had them beheaded at once.

manualTranslations.zh: 時遣兵討賊，集濟南，乏食，復亨盡出其私蓄以濟師，世祖嘉之，賜白金五千兩，復亨固辭。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time troops were sent to suppress the rebels and gathered at Jinan; provisions were short; Fuheng gave all his private stores to supply the army; Shizu praised him and granted five thousand taels of white silver; Fuheng firmly declined.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When imperial troops gathered at Jinan to suppress the rebels and food ran short, Fuheng gave his entire private store to feed the army. Kublai commended him and granted five thousand taels of white silver, but Fuheng firmly declined.

sourceRange.text: 好古字信甫，少讀書，善屬文，器識宏遠，勇而有謀。父晉亨權知東平府事，嚴忠濟承制以好古權其父軍，戍宿州。戊午，奏真授行軍千戶，攻樊城，身中流矢，戰不少卻，主將旌其功，賞銀百兩。略揚，循泰興、海門而還。擊邵伯埭，拔之。從大軍攻鄂。中統元年，還宿州，忠濟命兼恩州刺史，訪民瘼，革吏弊，立為條約。未幾，移戍蘄（州）〔縣〕。李璮叛，據濟南，宋人攻蘄，好古率兵迎擊，力不敵，死之。時晉亨在濟南軍中，聞之，哭曰：「吾兒死得其所矣。」弟好義襲，下江淮有功。王珍字國寶，大名南樂人，世為農家。珍慷慨有大志。

localRange.text: 王珍字國寶，大名南樂人，世為農家，珍慷慨有大志。

context.beforeSource: 子好古。
context.afterSource: 金末喪亂，所在盜起，南樂人楊鐵槍聚眾保鄉里。
context.beforeLocal: 子好古。
context.afterLocal: 金末喪亂，所在盜起，南樂人楊鐵槍，聚衆保鄉里。

manualTranslations.zh: 好古字信甫，少讀書，善屬文，器識宏遠，勇而有謀。
manualTranslations.literal: Haogu, courtesy name Xinfu, in youth read books, was skilled in composition, had broad vision and far-reaching judgment, and was brave and resourceful.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Haogu, whose courtesy name was Xinfu, read widely in his youth, wrote well, and showed broad vision together with courage and shrewdness.

manualTranslations.zh: 父晉亨權知東平府事，嚴忠濟承制以好古權其父軍，戍宿州。
manualTranslations.literal: His father Jinheng acted as provisional administrator of Dongping prefecture; Yan Zhongji acting by order had Haogu command his father's army and garrison Suzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father Jinheng was acting administrator of Dongping prefecture. Yan Zhongji, acting by order, put Haogu in command of his father's troops and posted him to garrison Suzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 戊午，奏真授行軍千戶，攻樊城，身中流矢，戰不少卻，主將旌其功，賞銀百兩。
manualTranslations.literal: In wuwu he memorialized for formal appointment as campaign thousand-household; attacking Fancheng he was struck by a flying arrow yet did not retreat in battle; the commanding general praised his merit and rewarded him with one hundred taels of silver.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 1258 he was formally appointed campaign thousand-household. At the assault on Fancheng he took an arrow wound yet never fell back. The commander commended him and rewarded him with one hundred taels of silver.

manualTranslations.zh: 略揚，循泰興、海門而還。
manualTranslations.literal: He raided Yang, followed Taixing and Haimen, and returned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He raided into Yangzhou, swept through Taixing and Haimen, and returned.

manualTranslations.zh: 擊邵伯埭，拔之。
manualTranslations.literal: He struck Shaobo Dam and took it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He attacked Shaobo Dam and captured it.

manualTranslations.zh: 從大軍攻鄂。
manualTranslations.literal: He followed the great army in attacking E.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He joined the main army in the attack on Ezhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 中統元年，還宿州，忠濟命兼恩州刺史，訪民瘼，革吏弊，立為條約。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong he returned to Suzhou; Zhongji ordered him to concurrently serve as prefect of Enzhou, inquire into the people's hardships, reform official abuses, and establish regulations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 1260 he returned to Suzhou. Zhongji made him concurrent prefect of Enzhou, where he investigated popular grievances, reformed official abuses, and set down regulations.

manualTranslations.zh: 未幾，移戍蘄縣。
manualTranslations.literal: Before long he was transferred to garrison Qixian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was reassigned to garrison Qixian.

manualTranslations.zh: 李璮叛，據濟南，宋人攻蘄，好古率兵迎擊，力不敵，死之。
manualTranslations.literal: Li Tan rebelled and held Jinan; Song men attacked Qi; Haogu led troops to meet the attack, strength did not match, and he died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Li Tan rebelled and held Jinan, Song forces attacked Qi. Haogu led his men out to meet them, was overpowered, and fell in battle.

manualTranslations.zh: 時晉亨在濟南軍中，聞之，哭曰：「吾兒死得其所矣。」
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Jinheng was in the Jinan army; hearing it he wept and said: "My son has died in the right place."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jinheng was then with the army at Jinan. When he heard the news he wept and said, "My son died where he ought."

manualTranslations.zh: 弟好義襲，下江淮有功。
manualTranslations.literal: His younger brother Haoyi inherited and, in subduing the Jiang-Huai region, had merit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His younger brother Haoyi succeeded him and won distinction in the Jiang-Huai campaigns.

manualTranslations.zh: 王珍字國寶，大名南樂人，世為農家，珍慷慨有大志。
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Zhen, courtesy name Guobao, was a man of Nanle in Daming; his family for generations were farmers; Zhen was generous and had great resolve.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen, whose courtesy name was Guobao, came from Nanle in Daming. His family had farmed for generations, but Zhen himself was openhanded and ambitious.

sourceRange.text: 懋字之美，未弱冠，已有父風。侍子良官京東，故懋領其眾，從丞相阿朮軍，立歸德府，以其軍鎮之。移鎮下邳，知歸德府事。李璮叛濟南，以其兵戍蔡州。中統元年，宣授泗州軍總把，佩金符。

context.beforeSource: 子鑑襲。
context.afterSource: 至元七年，擢濟南諸路新軍千戶。

manualTranslations.zh: 懋字之美，未弱冠，已有父風。
manualTranslations.literal: Mao, courtesy name Zhimei, before reaching capped adulthood already had his father's manner.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mao, whose courtesy name was Zhimei, showed his father's character even before he came of age.

manualTranslations.zh: 侍子良官京東，故懋領其眾，從丞相阿朮軍，立歸德府，以其軍鎮之。
manualTranslations.literal: As Ziliang attended to office in Jingdong, Mao therefore led his following, followed Chancellor A'zhu's army, established Guide prefecture, and garrisoned it with his troops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: While Zhang Ziliang was serving in Jingdong, Mao took command of his following, joined Chancellor A'zhu's army, helped establish Guide prefecture, and garrisoned it with his troops.

manualTranslations.zh: 移鎮下邳，知歸德府事。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to garrison Xiapi and served as administrator of Guide prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Xiapi and made administrator of Guide prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 李璮叛濟南，以其兵戍蔡州。
manualTranslations.literal: When Li Tan rebelled at Jinan, he used his troops to garrison Caizhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Li Tan rebelled at Jinan, Mao was posted with his troops to garrison Caizhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 中統元年，宣授泗州軍總把，佩金符。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong he was proclaimed and appointed chief commander of the Sizhou army, wearing a gold tally.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 1260 he was formally appointed chief commander of the Sizhou army and granted a gold tally.

sourceRange.text: 實卒，其（其）子忠濟奏晉亨權知東平府事。東平貢賦率倍他道，迎送供億，簿書獄訟，日不暇給，歷七年，吏畏而民安之。辛亥，憲宗即位，從忠濟入覲。時包銀制行，朝議戶賦銀六兩，諸道長吏有輒請試行於民者，晉亨面責之曰：「諸君職在親民，民之利病，且不知乎？今天顏咫尺，知而不言，罪也。承命而歸，事不克濟，罪當何如！且五方土產各異，隨其產為賦，則民便而易足，必責輸銀，雖破民之產，有不能辦者。」大臣以聞，明日召見，如其言以對，帝是之，乃得蠲戶額三之一，仍聽民輸他物，遂為定制。欲賜晉亨金虎符，辭曰：「虎符，國之名器，長一道者所佩，臣隸忠濟麾下，復佩虎符，非制也。臣不敢受。」帝益喜，改賜璽書、金符，恩州管民萬戶。

context.beforeSource: 大小數十戰，策功居多。
context.afterSource: 中統三年，李璮叛，晉亨從嚴忠範戰於遙牆濼，勝之，改本道奧魯萬戶。

manualTranslations.zh: 實卒，其子忠濟奏晉亨權知東平府事。
manualTranslations.literal: When Shi died, his son Zhongji memorialized that Jinheng should act as provisional administrator of Dongping prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yan Shi died, his son Zhongji memorialized to have Jinheng serve as acting administrator of Dongping prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 東平貢賦率倍他道，迎送供億，簿書獄訟，日不暇給，歷七年，吏畏而民安之。
manualTranslations.literal: Dongping's tribute and levies were generally double those of other circuits; receiving and escorting supplies, registers and lawsuits left no day unoccupied; over seven years officials feared him while the people were settled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dongping's tribute and levies were typically twice those of other circuits. Receiving envoys, supplying transport, and handling registers and lawsuits left him no spare day. For seven years officials feared him while the people lived in peace.

manualTranslations.zh: 辛亥，憲宗即位，從忠濟入覲。
manualTranslations.literal: In xinhai, when Emperor Xianzong took the throne, he followed Zhongji to audience.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 1251, when Emperor Xianzong succeeded, he accompanied Zhongji to court.

manualTranslations.zh: 時包銀制行，朝議戶賦銀六兩，諸道長吏有輒請試行於民者，晉亨面責之曰：「諸君職在親民，民之利病，且不知乎？
manualTranslations.literal: At that time the household-silver levy was in force; the court debated assessing six taels of silver per household; circuit chiefs who rashly asked to try it on the people—Jinheng rebuked them to their faces, saying: "Your duty is to be close to the people—do you not even know the people's hardships?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The household-silver levy was then in force, and the court debated a six-tael silver assessment per household. When circuit chiefs rashly proposed trying it on the people, Jinheng rebuked them face to face: "Your duty is to live among the people—do you not even know their hardships?

manualTranslations.zh: 今天顏咫尺，知而不言，罪也。
manualTranslations.literal: The imperial countenance is within a foot, yet knowing and not speaking is a crime."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor is right before us. To know this and say nothing is a crime."

manualTranslations.zh: 承命而歸，事不克濟，罪當何如！
manualTranslations.literal: Receiving the order and returning, if the task cannot be accomplished, what crime is fitting!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If we take the order home and the task fails, what punishment will we deserve!

manualTranslations.zh: 且五方土產各異，隨其產為賦，則民便而易足，必責輸銀，雖破民之產，有不能辦者。」
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover the products of the five regions differ; levying according to local products would make things convenient and easy to meet; if silver payment is required, even ruining the people's property, some cannot fulfill it."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Besides, products differ across the regions. Levying according to local produce would be convenient and easy to meet. If silver is required, some people will be ruined and still unable to pay."

manualTranslations.zh: 大臣以聞，明日召見，如其言以對，帝是之，乃得蠲戶額三之一，仍聽民輸他物，遂為定制。
manualTranslations.literal: The great ministers reported it; the next day he was summoned and answered as he had spoken; the emperor approved it; thereupon one-third of the household quota was remitted, and the people were still allowed to submit other goods—this then became fixed regulation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The ministers reported his words. The next day he was summoned and answered as he had argued. The emperor agreed, one-third of the household quota was remitted, and people were allowed to pay in other goods. This became standing policy.

manualTranslations.literal: Wishing to grant Jinheng a gold tiger tally, he declined, saying: "The tiger tally is a famous instrument of state; the chief of a circuit wears it. I serve under Zhongji; to wear a tiger tally again is not regulation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the emperor wished to grant him a gold tiger tally, he declined: "The tiger tally is a state emblem worn by a circuit chief. I serve under Zhongji. For me to wear one as well would be irregular.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣不敢受。」
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant dares not accept it."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I dare not accept it."

sourceRange.text: 己丑，太宗即位，改造行宮幄殿。乙未，城和林，建萬安宮，設宮闈司局，立驛傳，以便貢輸。既成，宴賜甚渥。辛丑春，授行尚書省，詔曰：「卿之所行，有司不得與聞。」俄而牙魯瓦赤自西域回，奏與敏同治漢民，帝允其請。牙魯瓦赤素剛尚氣，恥不得自專，遂俾其屬忙哥兒誣敏以流言，敏出手詔示之，乃已。帝聞之，命漢察火兒赤、中書左丞〔相〕粘合重山、奉御李簡詰問得實，罷牙魯瓦赤，仍令敏獨任。復辟李臻為左右司郎中，臻在幕府二十年，參贊之力居多。丙午，定宗即位，詔敏與奧都剌同行省事。辛亥夏六月，憲宗即位，召赴行在所，仍命與牙魯瓦赤同政。甲寅，請以子世亨自代，帝許之，賜世亨銀章，佩金虎符，賜名塔塔兒台。帝諭世亨以不從命者黜之。又賜其子世濟名散祝台，為必闍赤，入宿衞。

context.beforeSource: 興學校，進名士為之師。
context.afterSource: 帝伐宋，幸陝右，敏輿疾請見，帝曰：「卿有疾，不召而來，將有言乎？

manualTranslations.zh: 己丑，太宗即位，改造行宮幄殿。
manualTranslations.literal: In jichou, when Taizong took the throne, he rebuilt the traveling palace tent-hall.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In jichou, after Taizong acceded, he rebuilt the traveling palace tent-hall.

manualTranslations.zh: 乙未，城和林，建萬安宮，設宮闈司局，立驛傳，以便貢輸。
manualTranslations.literal: In yimao he walled Karakorum, built the Palace of Ten Thousand Peace, established the palace women's bureau, and set up post relays to facilitate tribute transport.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In yimao he fortified Karakorum, built the Palace of Ten Thousand Peace, established the palace women's bureau, and set up courier posts to ease tribute transport.

manualTranslations.zh: 既成，宴賜甚渥。
manualTranslations.literal: When it was finished, feasts and gifts were very generous.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the work was done, he feasted and rewarded his men with great generosity.

manualTranslations.zh: 辛丑春，授行尚書省，詔曰：「卿之所行，有司不得與聞。」
manualTranslations.literal: In the spring of xinchou he was put in charge of the traveling Secretariat; an edict said, "What you do—regular officials may not hear of it."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the spring of xinchou he was made head of the traveling Secretariat. The edict read, "What you undertake—regular officials are not to be informed."

manualTranslations.zh: 俄而牙魯瓦赤自西域回，奏與敏同治漢民，帝允其請。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon Yarluwachi returned from the Western Regions and memorialized that he and Min jointly govern the Han people; the Emperor granted his request.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon Yarluwachi returned from the west and asked to govern the Han people jointly with Min; the Emperor agreed.

manualTranslations.zh: 牙魯瓦赤素剛尚氣，恥不得自專，遂俾其屬忙哥兒誣敏以流言，敏出手詔示之，乃已。
manualTranslations.literal: Yarluwachi was by nature stubborn and proud of spirit; ashamed that he could not act alone, he had his subordinate Mangge'er slander Min with rumors. Min produced the imperial edict and showed it, and the matter ceased.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yarluwachi was proud and headstrong; shamed that he could not rule alone, he had his man Mangge'er spread rumors against Min. Min produced the imperial edict, and the slander stopped.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝聞之，命漢察火兒赤、中書左丞粘合重山、奉御李簡詰問得實，罷牙魯瓦赤，仍令敏獨任。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he ordered Hanzha Huo'erchi, Left Secretariat Chancellor Nianhe Zhongshan, and Palace Attendant Li Jian to investigate and establish the facts; Yarluwachi was dismissed and Min was left in sole charge.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Hanzha Huo'erchi, Left Secretariat Chancellor Nianhe Zhongshan, and Palace Attendant Li Jian to investigate. The facts were established, Yarluwachi was removed, and Min was left in sole charge.

manualTranslations.zh: 復辟李臻為左右司郎中，臻在幕府二十年，參贊之力居多。
manualTranslations.literal: Li Zhen was recalled as left-right Secretariat director; Zhen had been in the staff office twenty years, and his advisory contribution was greatest.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Zhen was recalled as director of the left and right secretariat offices; he had served in the staff office twenty years and had contributed more than anyone to its counsel.

manualTranslations.zh: 丙午，定宗即位，詔敏與奧都剌同行省事。
manualTranslations.literal: In bingwu, when Dingzong took the throne, an edict ordered Min and Otucar to administer traveling secretariat affairs together.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In bingwu, after Dingzong acceded, Min and Otucar were ordered to administer traveling secretariat affairs jointly.

manualTranslations.zh: 辛亥夏六月，憲宗即位，召赴行在所，仍命與牙魯瓦赤同政。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of summer in xinhai, when Xianzong took the throne, Min was summoned to the mobile court and again ordered to govern jointly with Yarluwachi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer in xinhai, after Xianzong acceded, Min was summoned to the mobile court and again ordered to share government with Yarluwachi.

manualTranslations.zh: 甲寅，請以子世亨自代，帝許之，賜世亨銀章，佩金虎符，賜名塔塔兒台。
manualTranslations.literal: In jiayin he asked that his son Shiheng replace him; the Emperor consented, gave Shiheng a silver seal, had him wear a gold tiger tally, and bestowed the name Tatartai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In jiayin he asked to be replaced by his son Shiheng. The Emperor agreed, gave Shiheng a silver seal and gold tiger tally, and bestowed on him the name Tatartai.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝諭世亨以不從命者黜之。
manualTranslations.literal: The Emperor instructed Shiheng to dismiss those who did not obey orders.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Shiheng to remove anyone who disobeyed orders.

manualTranslations.zh: 又賜其子世濟名散祝台，為必闍赤，入宿衞。
manualTranslations.literal: He also gave his son Shiji the name Sanzhutai, made him a bitan, and had him enter the imperial guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also gave his son Shiji the name Sanzhutai, made him a bitan, and enrolled him in the imperial guard.

manualTranslations.literal: Ji went altogether five times; because the peace talks were unresolved, hidden anxiety brought on illness, and he died in the south.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He went five times in all; the stalled peace talks preyed on him until illness took him, and he died in the south.

sourceRange.text: 辛丑，實子忠濟襲職，授左右司郎中，遂總行臺之政。分封之家，以嚴氏總握其事，頗不自便，定宗即位，皆聚闕下，復欲剖分東平地。是時，眾心危疑，將俛首聽命，玉汝力排羣言，事遂已。憲宗即位，有旨令常賦外，歲出銀六兩，謂之包垜銀。玉汝曰：「民力不支矣！」糾率諸路管民官，愬之闕下，得減三分之一。累官至龍虎衛上將軍、泰定軍節度使，兼兖州管內觀察使，充行臺參議。

context.afterSource: 壬子，以病謝事杜門，日以經史自娛。

manualTranslations.literal: In xinchou, Shi's son Zhongji inherited the post, was made left-right Secretariat director, and then oversaw traveling secretariat government.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In xinchou Yan Shi's son Zhongji inherited the post, was made director of the left and right secretariat offices, and took charge of the traveling secretariat.

manualTranslations.zh: 分封之家，以嚴氏總握其事，頗不自便，定宗即位，皆聚闕下，復欲剖分東平地。
manualTranslations.literal: Among enfeoffed households, the Yan clan held overall control of affairs, which was rather inconvenient; when Dingzong took the throne all were gathered at court and again wished to carve up the Dongping lands.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Among the enfeoffed houses the Yan clan held overall control, which many found awkward. When Dingzong acceded everyone was summoned to court, and they again sought to partition the Dongping territory.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時，眾心危疑，將俛首聽命，玉汝力排羣言，事遂已。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time hearts were fearful and doubtful and all were about to bow their heads and obey; Yuru forcefully rebutted the crowd, and the matter was dropped.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fear and doubt ran through the court and men were ready to submit, but Yuru forcefully rebutted the proposal and the partition was abandoned.

manualTranslations.zh: 憲宗即位，有旨令常賦外，歲出銀六兩，謂之包垜銀。
manualTranslations.literal: When Xianzong took the throne, an order required that beyond regular levies six taels of silver be paid each year, called baoduo silver.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Xianzong acceded, an order required six taels of silver beyond regular levies each year, called baoduo silver.

manualTranslations.zh: 玉汝曰：「民力不支矣！」
manualTranslations.literal: Yuru said, "The people's strength cannot bear it!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuru said, "The people cannot bear this!"

manualTranslations.zh: 糾率諸路管民官，愬之闕下，得減三分之一。
manualTranslations.literal: He rallied civilian administrators of every circuit and appealed at court, obtaining a reduction of one-third.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He rallied civilian administrators from every circuit and appealed at court, winning a reduction of one-third.

manualTranslations.zh: 累官至龍虎衛上將軍、泰定軍節度使，兼兖州管內觀察使，充行臺參議。
manualTranslations.literal: By cumulative promotion he reached General-in-Chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, military commissioner of the Taiding Army, concurrent observation commissioner within Yanzhou, and councilor of the traveling secretariat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He rose to general-in-chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, military commissioner of the Taiding Army, concurrent observation commissioner of Yanzhou, and councilor of the traveling secretariat.

sourceRange.text: 世祖即位，中統元年，授中書左右司郎中。從帝北征，每陳說資治通鑑，雖在軍中，未嘗廢書。一日，帝問：「郎俸幾何？」居貞以數對。帝謂其太薄，敕增之，居貞辭曰：「品秩宜然，不可以臣而紊制。」劉秉忠奏居貞為參知政事，又辭曰：「他日必有由郎官援例求執政者，將何以處之？」不拜。至元元年，參議中書省事，詔與左丞姚樞行省河東山西，罷侯置守。五年，再為中書郎中，時阿合馬擅權，忌之，改給事中。同丞相史天澤等纂修國史。

manualTranslations.zh: 世祖即位，中統元年，授中書左右司郎中。
manualTranslations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, in the first year of Zhongtong he was made director of the left and right secretariat offices of the Central Secretariat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Shizu acceded, in the first year of Zhongtong he was made director of the Central Secretariat's left and right offices.

manualTranslations.zh: 從帝北征，每陳說資治通鑑，雖在軍中，未嘗廢書。
manualTranslations.literal: Following the Emperor on the northern campaign, he lectured on the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government; though in the army, he never abandoned his books.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the northern campaign he lectured on the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government; even in camp he never set his books aside.

manualTranslations.zh: 一日，帝問：「郎俸幾何？」
manualTranslations.literal: One day the Emperor asked, "What is a director's salary?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: One day the Emperor asked, "What is a director's salary?"

manualTranslations.zh: 居貞以數對。
manualTranslations.literal: Juzhen answered with the figure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Juzhen gave the figure.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝謂其太薄，敕增之，居貞辭曰：「品秩宜然，不可以臣而紊制。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Emperor said it was too small and ordered an increase; Juzhen declined, saying, "Rank and salary ought to be as they are—one must not, as a subject, disorder the regulations."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Emperor called it too small and ordered an increase. Juzhen refused: "Rank and pay should stay as they are—a subject must not upset the regulations."

manualTranslations.zh: 劉秉忠奏居貞為參知政事，又辭曰：「他日必有由郎官援例求執政者，將何以處之？」
manualTranslations.literal: Liu Bingzhong memorialized to make Juzhen vice grand councilor; he again declined, saying, "Some day there will certainly be directors who cite this precedent to seek high office—how will you deal with them?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bingzhong recommended Juzhen as vice grand councilor. He refused again: "Directors will cite this precedent to seek high office—how will you answer them?"

manualTranslations.zh: 不拜。
manualTranslations.literal: He did not accept the appointment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He did not accept.

manualTranslations.zh: 至元元年，參議中書省事，詔與左丞姚樞行省河東山西，罷侯置守。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan he deliberated on Central Secretariat affairs; an edict ordered him with Left Chancellor Yao Shu to administer the Hedong and Shanxi branch secretariat, abolishing marquisates and establishing garrisons.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiyuan he became a deliberator of Central Secretariat affairs. He and Left Chancellor Yao Shu were sent to administer the Hedong and Shanxi branch secretariat, abolishing marquisates and establishing garrisons.

manualTranslations.zh: 五年，再為中書郎中，時阿合馬擅權，忌之，改給事中。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth year he again became Secretariat director; at that time Ahmad monopolized power, resented him, and had him transferred to palace secretary.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he again became a Secretariat director. Ahmad then held power, resented him, and had him transferred to palace secretary.

manualTranslations.zh: 同丞相史天澤等纂修國史。
manualTranslations.literal: Together with Chancellor Shi Tianze and others he compiled the national history.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: With Chancellor Shi Tianze and others he compiled the national history.

sourceRange.text: 子諒，裕宗初封燕王，以諒為符寶郎，俄命襲其父官，為鷹房都總管。裕宗甚愛之，謂符寶郎董文忠曰：「汝為我奏請，以諒所管民戶隸於我，庶得諒盡力為我用。」文忠入奏，帝從之。未幾，授諒嘉議大夫，遷兵部尚書。卒。仁宗時，贈推誠保德贊治功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封營國公，諡宣靖。子塔失不花，成宗命世其祖父官，以居喪辭。大德元年，授奉議大夫、章佩監丞。四年，改朝列大夫、利用監丞。八年，陞少監。武宗即位，授中議大夫、祕書監丞。仁宗居東宮，召入宿衞。至大三年冬，遷少中大夫、納綿府達魯花赤，且諭之曰：「此先世所守舊職也。」皇慶元年春，改授嘉議大夫、同知崇祥院事。冬，進資德大夫，為院使。

manualTranslations.zh: 子諒，裕宗初封燕王，以諒為符寶郎，俄命襲其父官，為鷹房都總管。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Liang—when Yuzong was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yan, Liang was made keeper of seals and tallies; soon he was ordered to inherit his father's office as chief director of the Falconry Office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Liang: when Yuzong was first made Prince of Yan, Liang was appointed keeper of seals and tallies, and soon ordered to inherit his father's post as chief director of the falconry office.

manualTranslations.zh: 裕宗甚愛之，謂符寶郎董文忠曰：「汝為我奏請，以諒所管民戶隸於我，庶得諒盡力為我用。」
manualTranslations.literal: Yuzong greatly favored him and said to Keeper of Seals Dong Wenzhong, "Memorialize for me that the households Liang governs be placed under me, so that Liang may exert himself fully in my service."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuzong favored him greatly and told Keeper of Seals Dong Wenzhong, "Memorialize for me that the households under Liang be assigned to me, so Liang will serve me with his full strength."

manualTranslations.zh: 文忠入奏，帝從之。
manualTranslations.literal: Wenzhong memorialized at court and the Emperor assented.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wenzhong memorialized and the Emperor agreed.

manualTranslations.zh: 未幾，授諒嘉議大夫，遷兵部尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: Before long Liang was given Grand Master of Exalted Counsel and transferred to minister of war.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon Liang was made Grand Master of Exalted Counsel and promoted to minister of war.

manualTranslations.zh: 卒。
manualTranslations.literal: He died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died.

manualTranslations.zh: 仁宗時，贈推誠保德贊治功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封營國公，諡宣靖。
manualTranslations.literal: In Renzong's time he was posthumously given the title Meritous Subject Who Promotes Sincerity, Preserves Virtue, and Assists Governance, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master of Honor Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Pillar of the State, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Ying, with the posthumous title Solemn and Tranquil.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Renzong he was posthumously honored as Meritous Subject Who Promotes Sincerity, Preserves Virtue, and Assists Governance, grand preceptor, grand master of honor equal to the three excellencies, and pillar of the state, enfeoffed as Duke of Ying, with the posthumous title Solemn and Tranquil.

manualTranslations.zh: 子塔失不花，成宗命世其祖父官，以居喪辭。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Taishibuhua—Chengzong ordered him to inherit his grandfather's office, but he declined on grounds of mourning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Taishibuhua was ordered by Chengzong to inherit his grandfather's office but declined while in mourning.

manualTranslations.zh: 大德元年，授奉議大夫、章佩監丞。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Dade he was given Grand Master of Discussion and made vice director of the Seal and Girdle Office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dade he was made Grand Master of Discussion and vice director of the Seal and Girdle Office.

manualTranslations.zh: 四年，改朝列大夫、利用監丞。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth year he was changed to Grand Master of Court Audience and made vice director of the Utilization Office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became Grand Master of Court Audience and vice director of the Utilization Office.

manualTranslations.zh: 八年，陞少監。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to vice director.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to vice director.

manualTranslations.zh: 武宗即位，授中議大夫、祕書監丞。
manualTranslations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne he was given Grand Master of Central Counsel and made vice director of the Secretariat Library.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Wuzong acceded he was made Grand Master of Central Counsel and vice director of the Secretariat Library.

manualTranslations.zh: 仁宗居東宮，召入宿衞。
manualTranslations.literal: When Renzong resided in the Eastern Palace he was summoned into the imperial guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: While Renzong was heir apparent he was summoned into the imperial guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 至大三年冬，遷少中大夫、納綿府達魯花赤，且諭之曰：「此先世所守舊職也。」
manualTranslations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Zhide he was transferred to Junior Grand Master of the Center and darughachi of the Nayuan Office, and was told, "This is the hereditary post your forebears held."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year of Zhide he became junior grand master of the center and darughachi of the Nayuan Office, and was told, "This is the hereditary post your family has held."

manualTranslations.zh: 皇慶元年春，改授嘉議大夫、同知崇祥院事。
manualTranslations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Huangqing he was reassigned as Grand Master of Exalted Counsel and vice director of the Chongxiang Office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Huangqing he was reassigned as Grand Master of Exalted Counsel and vice director of the Chongxiang Office.

manualTranslations.zh: 冬，進資德大夫，為院使。
manualTranslations.literal: In winter he was advanced to Grand Master of Assisting Virtue and made director of the office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That winter he was promoted to Grand Master of Assisting Virtue and made director of the office.

sourceRange.text: 三十年，除湖廣行樞密副使。湖南地闊遠，羣寇依險出沒，昭、賀二州及廬陵境，民常被害。制宜率偏師徇二州，道經廬陵永新，獲首賊及其黨，皆殺之。茶鄉譚計龍者，聚惡少年，匿兵器為姦，既捕獲，其家納賂以緩獄事，制宜悉以勞軍，斬計龍于市，自是湖以南無復盜賊。元貞元年，有制：行樞密院添置副使一員，與制宜連署。制宜以員非常設，先任者當罷。俄入朝，特授大都留守，領少府監，兼武衞親軍都指揮使，知屯田事。

context.beforeSource: 制宜奉詔而往，按圖籍以正之，訟由是息。

manualTranslations.zh: 三十年，除湖廣行樞密副使。
manualTranslations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was appointed vice military affairs commissioner of the Huguang Branch Military Affairs Commission.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he was made vice military affairs commissioner of the Huguang Branch Military Affairs Commission.

manualTranslations.zh: 湖南地闊遠，羣寇依險出沒，昭、賀二州及廬陵境，民常被害。
manualTranslations.literal: Hunan was broad and remote; bandits relied on rugged terrain to appear and disappear. In Zhao and He prefectures and the Luling region, the people were often harmed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hunan was vast and remote, and bandits used the rugged terrain to raid at will. The people of Zhao and He prefectures and the Luling region suffered constantly.

manualTranslations.zh: 制宜率偏師徇二州，道經廬陵永新，獲首賊及其黨，皆殺之。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhiyi led a detached force to pacify the two prefectures. Passing through Yongxin in Luling, he captured the chief bandit and his followers and executed them all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhiyi led a detached column to pacify the two prefectures. On the road through Yongxin in Luling he captured the ringleader and his band and put them all to death.

manualTranslations.zh: 茶鄉譚計龍者，聚惡少年，匿兵器為姦，既捕獲，其家納賂以緩獄事，制宜悉以勞軍，斬計龍于市，自是湖以南無復盜賊。
manualTranslations.literal: In Chaxiang there was Tan Jilong, who gathered wicked youths, hid weapons, and committed outrages. Once captured, his family offered bribes to delay the case. Zhiyi used the money entirely to reward the troops and beheaded Jilong in the market. From then on south of the lake there were no more bandits.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Chaxiang one Tan Jilong had gathered unruly youths, hidden weapons, and committed crimes. After his capture his family tried to bribe their way out of prosecution. Zhiyi gave the bribes entirely to the troops as reward, executed Jilong in the market, and from then on banditry south of the lake ceased.

manualTranslations.zh: 元貞元年，有制：行樞密院添置副使一員，與制宜連署。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen an order was issued: the branch military affairs commission was to add one vice commissioner to serve jointly with Zhiyi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanzhen an edict ordered the branch military affairs commission to add one vice commissioner to serve jointly with Zhiyi.

manualTranslations.zh: 制宜以員非常設，先任者當罷。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhiyi held that the post was not a permanent establishment and that the incumbent should be dismissed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhiyi argued that the post was not a standing office and that the previous appointee should be removed.

manualTranslations.zh: 俄入朝，特授大都留守，領少府監，兼武衞親軍都指揮使，知屯田事。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he came to court and was specially appointed metropolitan prefect, director of the Court of Imperial Manufactories, and concurrently commander of the Martial Guard Imperial Guard with charge of garrison-farming affairs.

sourceRange.text: 中統元年，佩金虎符，為總管。三年，李璮叛，詔溫以軍還討。至濟南，大軍圍其城，賊將楊拔都等乘夜斫營，溫力戰至黎明，賊退，諸王哈必赤、丞相史天澤厚賞之。七月，城破，命溫率兵三千，往定益都。以功復受上賞，命為侍衞親軍總管。

context.beforeSource: 還至閬州，奉旨分軍守邏青居、釣魚等山，天澤命溫統四千人，警邏釣魚山。
context.afterSource: 至元六年，進懷遠大將軍、右衞副都指揮使。

manualTranslations.zh: 中統元年，佩金虎符，為總管。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong he wore the golden tiger tally and served as commander-in-chief.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong he was granted the golden tiger tally and appointed commander-in-chief.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年，李璮叛，詔溫以軍還討。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year Li Tan rebelled, and an edict ordered Wen to return with the army to suppress him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third year, when Li Tan rebelled, an edict ordered Wen to bring his troops back to suppress the revolt.

manualTranslations.zh: 至濟南，大軍圍其城，賊將楊拔都等乘夜斫營，溫力戰至黎明，賊退，諸王哈必赤、丞相史天澤厚賞之。
manualTranslations.literal: When they reached Jinan the main army besieged the city. The rebel generals Yang Badu and others struck the camp by night. Wen fought hard until dawn; the rebels withdrew, and Prince Qabochi and Chief Councilor Shi Tianze richly rewarded him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Jinan the main army besieged the city. Rebel generals including Yang Badu raided the camp by night. Wen fought until dawn and drove them off; Prince Qabochi and Chief Councilor Shi Tianze gave him a rich reward.

manualTranslations.zh: 七月，城破，命溫率兵三千，往定益都。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month the city fell. Wen was ordered to lead three thousand troops to pacify Yidu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the city fell, and Wen was ordered to lead three thousand men to pacify Yidu.

manualTranslations.zh: 以功復受上賞，命為侍衞親軍總管。
manualTranslations.literal: For merit he again received the highest reward and was appointed commander of the Personal Guard Imperial Guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For his service he again received the highest reward and was appointed commander of the Personal Guard Imperial Guard.

sourceRange.text: 世祖即位，入為侍衞親軍。中統二年，宣授總把，賜銀符。三年，從征李璮有功。至元八年，領兵赴襄陽。十二年，從略地湖北、湖南。宋平，以兵馬使分兵屯鄂州。十三年，領軍二千，屯田河西中興府。十四年，加武略將軍，陞千戶。十五年，移屯六盤山，加武毅將軍，賜金符。十七年，陞明威將軍、管軍總管。十九年，賜虎符，復進懷遠大將軍，命屯田西域別石八里。二十三年秋，海都及篤娃等領軍至洪水山，進與力戰，眾寡不敵，軍潰，進被擒。從至摻八里，遁還。至和州，收潰兵三百餘人，且戰且行，還至京師，賞金織紋衣二襲、鈔一千五百貫。二十五年，授蒙古侍衞親軍都指揮使司僉事。明年，改授左翼屯田萬戶。元貞元年春，卒。

context.beforeSource: 八月，又戰浮圖關，前後凡五戰，皆以功受上賞。
context.afterSource: 子雯，襲授武德將軍、左翼屯田萬戶，佩虎符。

manualTranslations.zh: 世祖即位，入為侍衞親軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Jin entered service in the Personal Guard Imperial Guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Kublai took the throne, Jin entered the Personal Guard Imperial Guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 中統二年，宣授總把，賜銀符。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong he was formally appointed chief corporal and granted a silver tally.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong he was formally appointed chief corporal and granted a silver tally.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年，從征李璮有功。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year he followed the campaign against Li Tan and had merit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third year he took part in the campaign against Li Tan and distinguished himself.

manualTranslations.zh: 至元八年，領兵赴襄陽。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan he led troops to Xiangyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan he led troops to Xiangyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 十二年，從略地湖北、湖南。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth year he followed in seizing territory in Hubei and Hunan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he took part in the conquest of Hubei and Hunan.

manualTranslations.zh: 宋平，以兵馬使分兵屯鄂州。
manualTranslations.literal: When Song was pacified he served as horse-and-troop commissioner and divided troops to garrison Ezhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the fall of Song he served as horse-and-troop commissioner and posted detachments to garrison Ezhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 十三年，領軍二千，屯田河西中興府。
manualTranslations.literal: In the thirteenth year he led two thousand troops to farm garrison lands in Hexi at Zhongxing Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he led two thousand men in garrison farming at Zhongxing Prefecture in Hexi.

manualTranslations.zh: 十四年，加武略將軍，陞千戶。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was advanced to Martial Stratagem General and promoted to thousand-household.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was made Martial Stratagem General and promoted to thousand-household.

manualTranslations.zh: 十五年，移屯六盤山，加武毅將軍，賜金符。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifteenth year he moved his garrison to Liupan Mountain, was advanced to Martial Resolution General, and granted a gold tally.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he shifted his garrison to Liupan Mountain, was made Martial Resolution General, and granted a gold tally.

manualTranslations.zh: 十七年，陞明威將軍、管軍總管。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was advanced to Martial Brilliance General and troop commander-in-chief.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Martial Brilliance General and troop commander-in-chief.

manualTranslations.zh: 十九年，賜虎符，復進懷遠大將軍，命屯田西域別石八里。
manualTranslations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was granted a tiger tally, again advanced to General of Cherished Distance, and ordered to farm garrison lands at Bieshibali in the Western Regions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he received a tiger tally, was again promoted to General of Cherished Distance, and ordered to farm garrison lands at Bieshibali in the Western Regions.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十三年秋，海都及篤娃等領軍至洪水山，進與力戰，眾寡不敵，軍潰，進被擒。
manualTranslations.literal: In autumn of the twenty-third year Qaidu and Duwa and others led troops to Hongshui Mountain. Jin fought them with all his strength, but being outnumbered his army collapsed and Jin was captured.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the twenty-third year Qaidu, Duwa, and others led troops to Hongshui Mountain. Jin fought hard but was outnumbered; his force broke and he was taken prisoner.

manualTranslations.zh: 從至摻八里，遁還。
manualTranslations.literal: He was taken as far as Sanbali, then escaped and returned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was carried as far as Sanbali before escaping and making his way back.

manualTranslations.zh: 至和州，收潰兵三百餘人，且戰且行，還至京師，賞金織紋衣二襲、鈔一千五百貫。
manualTranslations.literal: Reaching Hezhou, he gathered more than three hundred scattered troops, fought as he marched, and returned to the capital. He was rewarded with two suits of gold brocade robes and one thousand five hundred strings of paper money.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Hezhou he rallied more than three hundred scattered troops, fought his way back, and returned to the capital. He was rewarded with two suits of gold brocade robes and fifteen hundred strings of paper money.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十五年，授蒙古侍衞親軍都指揮使司僉事。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed secretarial aide of the Mongol Personal Guard Imperial Guard Metropolitan Command.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed secretarial aide of the Mongol Personal Guard Imperial Guard Metropolitan Command.

manualTranslations.zh: 明年，改授左翼屯田萬戶。
manualTranslations.literal: The next year he was reassigned as Left-Wing Agricultural Garrison Ten-Thousand-Household.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The following year he was reassigned as Left-Wing Agricultural Garrison Ten-Thousand-Household.

manualTranslations.zh: 元貞元年春，卒。
manualTranslations.literal: In spring of the first year of Yuanzhen he died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Yuanzhen he died.

sourceRange.text: 至元元年，加光祿大夫，右丞相如故。三年，皇太子燕王領中書省，兼判樞密院事，以天澤為輔國上將軍、樞密副使。四年，復授光祿大夫，改中書左丞相。六年，帝以宋未附，議攻襄陽，詔天澤與駙馬忽剌出往經畫之，賜白金百錠、楮幣萬緡。至則相要害，立城堡，以絕其聲援，為必取之計。七年，以疾還燕。八年，進開府儀同三司、平章軍國重事，仍敕右丞相安童諭旨曰：「兩省、院、臺，或一月、一旬，遇大事，卿可商量，小事不煩卿也。

context.beforeSource: 」於是史氏子姪即日解兵符者十七人。
context.afterSource: 」十年春，與平章阿朮等進攻樊城，拔之，襄陽降。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: In jichou, when Taizong succeeded, the court debated creating ten-thousand-household commands to lead Han troops in divided formations.

manualTranslations.zh: 天澤適入覲，命為真定、河間、大名、東平、濟南五路萬戶。
manualTranslations.literal: Tianze happened to be at court for an audience and was appointed ten-thousand-household commander of the five circuits of Zhending, Hejian, Daming, Dongping, and Jinan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tianze happened to be at court and was named commander of ten-thousand households over Zhending, Hejian, Daming, Dongping, and Jinan.

manualTranslations.zh: 庚寅冬，武仙復屯兵於衞，天澤合諸軍圍之。
manualTranslations.literal: In winter of gengyin Wu Xian again stationed troops at Wei; Tianze joined all armies to besiege him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That gengyin winter Wu Xian reoccupied Wei; Tianze combined the armies to besiege him.

manualTranslations.zh: 金將完顏合達以眾十萬來援，戰不利，諸將皆北，天澤獨以千人繞出其後，敗一都尉軍，與大軍合攻之，仙逸去，遂復衞州。
manualTranslations.literal: Jin general Wanyan Heda came with one hundred thousand to relieve them; the battle went ill; all generals retreated north; Tianze alone with one thousand men circled around behind them, defeated one commandant's army, joined the great army in attack, Xian fled away, and Weizhou was recovered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Jin general Wanyan Heda brought one hundred thousand men to relieve the city; when the fighting went badly and the other commanders withdrew north, Tianze alone took one thousand men around the enemy rear, routed a commandant's force, rejoined the main army, and drove Wu Xian off, recovering Weizhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 壬辰春，太宗由白坡渡河，詔天澤以兵由孟津會河南，至則睿宗已破合達軍于三峰山。
manualTranslations.literal: In spring of the renchen year Emperor Taizong crossed from Baipo; he ordered Tianze to lead troops from Mengjin to join Henan; when he arrived Prince Ruizong had already broken Heda's army at Sanfengshan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In renchen spring Taizong crossed at Baipo and ordered Tianze to join the Henan front via Mengjin; by the time he arrived, Prince Tolui had already crushed Heda at Sanfengshan.

sourceRange.text: 至元元年，弘略既入宿衞，帝召見，意其兄弟有可代守順天者，且念弘範有濟南之功，授順天路管民總管，佩金虎符。二年，移守大名。歲大水，漂沒廬舍，租稅無從出，弘範輒免之。朝廷罪其專擅，弘範請入見，進曰：「臣以為朝廷儲小倉，不若儲之大倉。」帝曰：「何說也？」對曰：「今歲水潦不收，而必責民輸，倉庫雖實，而民死亡殆盡，明年租將安出？曷若活其民，使不致逃亡，則歲有恒收，非陛下大倉庫乎！」帝曰：「知體，其勿問。

sourceRange.text: 士元，一名不花，字長卿，文炳長子也。自襁褓喪母，祖母李氏愛之，謂文炳曰：「俟兒能言，即令讀書。」數歲，從名儒受學。及長，善騎射。憲宗征蜀，士元年二十三，從叔父文蔚率鄧州一軍西行。師次釣魚山，宋人堅壁拒守。士元請代文蔚攻之，以所部銳卒先登，力戰良久，以它軍不繼而還。憲宗壯之，賜以金帛。

sourceRange.text: 秉忠雖居左右，而猶不改舊服，時人稱之為聰書記。至元元年，翰林學士承旨王鶚奏言：「秉忠久侍藩邸，積有歲年，參帷幄之密謀，定社稷之大計，忠勤勞績，宜被褒崇。聖明御極，萬物惟新，而秉忠猶仍其野服散號，深所未安，宜正其衣冠，崇以顯秩。」帝覽奏，即日拜光祿大夫，位太保，參（預）〔領〕中書省事。詔以翰林侍讀學士竇默之女妻之，賜第奉先坊，且以少府宮籍監戶給之。秉忠既受命，以天下為己任，事無巨細，凡有關於國家大體者，知無不言，言無不聽，帝寵任愈隆。燕閑顧問，輒推薦人物可備器使者，凡所甄拔，後悉為名臣。

sourceRange.text: 會宋守帥賈似道亦遣間使請和，迺班師。明年，世祖即位，以經為翰林侍讀學士，佩金虎符，充國信使使宋，告即位，且定和議，仍敕沿邊諸將毋鈔掠。經入辭，賜蒲萄酒，詔曰：「朕初即位，庶事草創，卿當遠行，凡可輔朕者，亟以聞。」經奏便宜十六事，皆立政大要，辭多不載。

sourceRange.text: 歲辛亥，憲宗即位。文謙與秉忠數以時務所當先者言於世祖，悉施行之。世祖征大理，國主高祥拒命，殺信使遁去。世祖怒，將屠其城。文謙與秉忠、姚樞諫曰：「殺使拒命者高祥爾，非民之罪，請宥之。」由是大理之民賴以全活。己未，世祖帥師伐宋，文謙與秉忠言：「王者之師，有征無戰，當一視同仁，不可嗜殺。」世祖曰：「期與卿等守此言。」既入宋境，分命諸將毋妄殺，毋焚人室廬，所獲生口悉縱之。

sourceRange.text: 憲宗即位，詔凡軍民在赤老溫山南者，聽世祖總之。世祖既奉詔，宴羣下，罷酒將出，遣人止樞，問曰：「頃者諸臣皆賀，汝獨默然，何耶？」對曰：「今天下土地之廣，人民之殷，財賦之阜，有加漢地者乎？軍民吾盡有之，天子何為？異時廷臣間之，必悔而見奪，不若惟持兵權，供億之需取之有司，則勢順理安。」世祖曰：「慮所不及者。」乃以聞，憲宗從之。樞又請置屯田經略司於汴以圖宋；置都運司于衞，轉粟于河。憲宗大封同姓，敕世祖於南京、關中自擇其一。樞曰：「南京河徙無常，土薄水淺，舄鹵生之，不若關中厥田上上，古名天府陸海。」於是世祖願有關中。

sourceRange.text: 衡善教，其言煦煦，雖與童子語，如恐傷之。故所至，無貴賤賢不肖皆樂從之，隨其才昏明大小皆有所得，可以為世用。所去，人皆哭泣，不忍舍，服念其教如金科玉條，終身不敢忘。或未嘗及門，傳其緒餘，而折節力行為名世者，往往有之。聽其言，雖武人俗士異端之徒，無不感悟者。丞相安童一見衡，語同列曰：「若輩自謂不相上下，蓋十百與千萬也。」翰林承旨王磐氣概一世，少所與可，獨見衡曰：「先生，神明也。」大德（二）〔元〕年，贈榮祿大夫、司徒，諡文正。至大二年，加正學垂憲佐運功臣、太傅、開府儀同三司，封魏國公。皇慶二年，詔從祀孔子廟廷。延祐初，又詔立書院京兆以祀衡，給田奉祠事，名魯齋書院。魯，衡居魏時所署齋名也。子師可。

sourceRange.text: 九年，封皇子忙阿剌為安西王，立王相府，以挺為王相。十四年，詔王北征，王命挺曰：「關中事有不便者，可悉更張之。」挺曰：「延安民兵數千，宜使李忽蘭吉練習之，以備不虞。」未幾，禿魯叛，以延安兵應敵，果獲其力。挺進十策於王，曰：睦親鄰，安人心，敬民時，備不虞，厚民生，一事權，清心源，謹自治，固本根，察下情。王為置酒嘉納。王薨，王妃使挺請命于朝，以子阿難答嗣。帝曰：「年少，祖宗之訓未習，卿姑行王相府事。」初，運使郭琮、郎中郭叔雲與王相趙炳搆隙。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon Tulü rebelled; the Yan'an troops were sent against him and proved their worth.

sourceRange.text: 憲宗崩，世祖即位。中統元年，拜燕京宣慰使。時供給蜀軍，府庫已竭，及用兵北邊，璧經畫饋運，相繼不絕。中書省立，授平章政事，議加答剌罕之號，力辭不受。二年，從北征，命還燕，以平章政事兼大都督領諸軍。是年，始製太廟雅樂。樂工党仲和、郭伯達以知音律在選中，為造偽鈔者連坐，繫獄。璧曰：「太廟雅樂，大饗用之，聖上所以昭孝報本也，豈可繫及無辜，而廢雅樂之成哉！」奏請原之。三年，李璮反益都，從親王合必赤討之。璮已據濟南，諸軍乏食，璧從濟河得粟及羊豕以饋軍，軍復大振。至元元年，官制行，加榮祿大夫。帝欲作文檄宋，執筆者數人，不稱旨，乃召璧為之。文成，帝大喜曰：「惟秀才曲盡我意。」改樞密副使。六年，宋守臣有遣間使約降者，帝命璧詣鹿門山都元帥阿朮營密議。命璧同行漢軍都元帥府事。宋將夏貴率兵五萬，饋糧三千艘，自武昌泝流，入援襄陽。時漢水暴漲，璧據險設伏待之。貴果中夜潛上，璧策馬出鹿門，行二十餘里，發伏兵，奪其五舟，大呼曰：「南船已敗，我水軍宜速進。」貴懾不敢動。明旦，阿朮至，領諸將渡江西追貴騎兵，璧率水軍萬戶解汝楫等追貴舟師。遂合戰於虎尾洲，貴大敗走，士卒溺死甚眾，奪戰艦五十，擒將士三百餘人。
